_note: Hand-checked 'Did you know' facts for Benflix title pages and the screensaver. Key: "Name (Year)" as Jellyfin shows it, or an IMDb number like "tt4589218". Keep each fact under about 170 characters, true, family-friendly and spoiler-free. Tower downloads this file every night.
Five Nights at Freddy's (2023): The animatronics in Five Nights at Freddy's are real, not computer-made. They were built by Jim Henson's Creature Shop.
Foxy was the hardest animatronic to work, needing a team of puppeteers to bring him to life.
Getting performers into the heavy animatronic suits first took about an hour. The crew got it down to a few minutes.
Scott Cawthon, who made the original Five Nights at Freddy's games, co-wrote the movie's script.
YouTuber MatPat, famous for his Game Theory videos about the games, has a cameo as a diner waiter.
YouTuber CoryxKenshin, who played the games on his channel, makes a cameo as a taxi driver.
Five Nights at Freddy's came out in theaters and on Peacock on the same day, and still became Blumhouse's biggest opening ever.
10 Items or Less (2006): 10 Items or Less was made on a tiny budget and filmed in about two weeks.
Morgan Freeman's own company, Revelations Entertainment, helped make 10 Items or Less.
13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghaz: Members of the real security team worked with the 13 Hours crew to get the details right.
13 Hours was filmed mostly in Malta, with Morocco also standing in for Libya.
2 Guns (2013): 2 Guns is based on a comic book series by Steven Grant from Boom! Studios.
21 (2008): 21 is based on Ben Mezrich's book Bringing Down the House, about a real MIT blackjack team.
Jeff Ma, the real MIT student the movie's hero is based on, has a cameo as a blackjack dealer.
50/50 (2011): 50/50 is based on writer Will Reiser's own fight with cancer in his twenties.
Seth Rogen really was Will Reiser's friend while he was sick, and the movie's best friend is based on him.
Joseph Gordon-Levitt really shaved his head on camera for 50/50, so they only had one take.
A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood (201: Tom Hanks found out he is a distant cousin of Fred Rogers, the man he plays.
A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood was filmed in Pittsburgh, including the real studio where Mister Rogers' Neighborhood was made.
The movie grew out of Tom Junod's 1998 Esquire magazine story about meeting Fred Rogers.
About Time (2013): Richard Curtis, who wrote Love Actually and Notting Hill, said About Time would be the last movie he directed.
Much of About Time was filmed in Cornwall, on England's southwest coast.
Absolution (2024): Absolution reunites Liam Neeson with director Hans Petter Moland, who also directed him in Cold Pursuit.
13 Going on 30 (2004): Brie Larson, years before Captain Marvel, has a small role in 13 Going on 30 as one of the popular girls.
17 Again (2009): Zac Efron and Matthew Perry play the same man in 17 Again: Efron as the teenage version, Perry as the grown-up.
27 Dresses (2008): 27 Dresses was written by Aline Brosh McKenna, who also wrote The Devil Wears Prada.
50 First Dates (2004): 50 First Dates was filmed in Hawaii, mostly on the island of Oahu.
9 (2009): 9 grew out of Shane Acker's short film of the same name, which was nominated for an Oscar.
Tim Burton was one of the producers of 9.
Adrift (2018): Adrift tells the true story of Tami Oldham, who sailed a wrecked yacht for 41 days to reach Hawaii.
Adrift was filmed out on the open ocean near Fiji, and Shailene Woodley did a lot of her own sailing.
A Bronx Tale (1993): A Bronx Tale was Robert De Niro's first movie as a director.
A Bronx Tale began as Chazz Palminteri's one-man stage show about his own childhood in the Bronx.
A Christmas Carol (1951): In Britain, the 1951 A Christmas Carol came out under the name Scrooge.
Alastair Sim's Scrooge in this version is often called the best ever put on film.
A Fish Called Wanda (1988): Kevin Kline won an Oscar for playing Otto in A Fish Called Wanda.
John Cleese wrote A Fish Called Wanda and co-directed it with Charles Crichton, a veteran of classic British comedies.
After Earth (2013): The story idea for After Earth came from Will Smith, who stars next to his real son Jaden.
Airheads (1994): The rock band White Zombie makes a cameo in Airheads.
Amadeus (1984): Amadeus won eight Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Actor for F. Murray Abraham.
Amadeus was filmed in Prague, which still had the old streets and theaters to stand in for Mozart's Vienna.
American Hustle (2013): American Hustle is loosely based on ABSCAM, a real FBI sting operation in the late 1970s.
Christian Bale gained about 40 pounds and hurt his back playing Irving Rosenfeld.
American Movie: The Making of Northweste: American Movie follows a real Wisconsin filmmaker, Mark Borchardt, trying to finish a tiny horror movie. It won the top documentary prize at Sundance.
American Ultra (2015): American Ultra was written by Max Landis, who also wrote Chronicle.
American Underdog (2021): Before he became an NFL star, the real Kurt Warner stocked shelves at a grocery store, just like in American Underdog.
Amy (2015): Amy won the Oscar for Best Documentary. It was made by Asif Kapadia, who also made the racing film Senna.
Angel Has Fallen (2019): Nick Nolte joins the series in Angel Has Fallen as Mike Banning's father.
Angels in the Outfield (1994): Angels in the Outfield is a remake of a 1951 movie with the same name.
A young Joseph Gordon-Levitt stars in Angels in the Outfield, and Matthew McConaughey and Adrien Brody have small roles.
Anger Management (2003): Anger Management is full of cameos, including tennis star John McEnroe and basketball coach Bobby Knight.
Aniara (2018): Aniara is based on a 1956 Swedish poem by Harry Martinson, who later won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Annihilation (2018): Alex Garland wrote Annihilation from his memory of Jeff VanderMeer's novel, without rereading the book.
Outside the US and China, Annihilation went straight to Netflix instead of cinemas.
Around the World in 80 Days (2004): Jackie Chan plays Passepartout in this Around the World in 80 Days, and did his own stunts.
Arnold Schwarzenegger has a cameo as Prince Hapi.
Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me (1: Mike Myers plays three parts in this Austin Powers: Austin, Dr. Evil and Fat Bastard.
Mini-Me is played by Verne Troyer, who was 2 feet 8 inches tall.
Baby Mama (2008): Tina Fey and Amy Poehler were already a famous team from hosting Weekend Update together on Saturday Night Live.
Bad Teacher (2011): Cameron Diaz and Justin Timberlake had dated for years before they played love interests in Bad Teacher.
Barbarian (2022): Barbarian's writer and director, Zach Cregger, started out in the comedy group The Whitest Kids U' Know.
BASEketball (1998): BASEketball stars Trey Parker and Matt Stone, the creators of South Park, and was directed by Airplane!'s David Zucker.
Beavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe (20: Mike Judge voices both Beavis and Butt-Head, just as he did in the 1990s.
Bedazzled (2000): Bedazzled is a remake of a 1967 British comedy starring Dudley Moore and Peter Cook. Groundhog Day's Harold Ramis directed it.
Bee Movie (2007): Jerry Seinfeld came up with Bee Movie from a silly pun he made over dinner with Steven Spielberg.
Jerry Seinfeld co-wrote Bee Movie and voices Barry B. Benson.
Beerfest (2006): Beerfest was made by Broken Lizard, the same comedy team behind Super Troopers.
Beethoven (1992): John Hughes co-wrote Beethoven under a made-up name, Edmond Dantès, the hero of The Count of Monte Cristo.
Bicentennial Man (1999): Bicentennial Man is based on a story by science fiction writer Isaac Asimov.
Big Daddy (1999): Twins Cole and Dylan Sprouse shared the role of Julian in Big Daddy, years before The Suite Life of Zack and Cody.
Big Fat Liar (2002): Much of Big Fat Liar was filmed on the real Universal Studios lot in Hollywood.
Billy Madison (1995): Billy Madison was Adam Sandler's first big starring role. He wrote it with his friend Tim Herlihy.
Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emanc: Margot Robbie pitched the idea of a Harley Quinn girl-gang movie to Warner Bros. herself, and produced it.
Blade II (2002): Blade II was directed by Guillermo del Toro, just before he made Hellboy.
Blazing Saddles (1974): Richard Pryor was one of the writers of Blazing Saddles.
Mel Brooks plays two parts in Blazing Saddles, including the silly Governor Le Petomane.
Blended (2014): Blended is Adam Sandler and Drew Barrymore's third movie together, after The Wedding Singer and 50 First Dates.
Blended was filmed in South Africa.
Blink Twice (2024): Blink Twice was Zoë Kravitz's first movie as a director.
Bo Burnham: Inside (2021): Bo Burnham made Inside completely alone in one room of his guest house, over about a year.
Breach (2007): Breach tells the true story of Robert Hanssen, an FBI agent who secretly spied for Moscow for over 20 years.
Bright (2017): At around $90 million, Bright was one of Netflix's most expensive movies when it came out.
Brightburn (2019): Brightburn was produced by James Gunn and written by his brother Brian and cousin Mark.
Brink! (1998): Brink! was a Disney Channel Original Movie about inline skating.
Bullet Train (2022): Bullet Train is based on the Japanese novel Maria Beetle by Kōtarō Isaka.
Bulletproof Monk (2003): Bulletproof Monk is based on a comic book from Flypaper Press.
Casper (1995): Casper was one of the first movies to have a main character made completely by computer.
Cats & Dogs (2001): Cats & Dogs mixed real trained animals with puppets and computer effects.
Cave of Forgotten Dreams (2010): Werner Herzog filmed Cave of Forgotten Dreams in 3D inside France's Chauvet Cave, where only a tiny crew was allowed in for short visits.
Central Intelligence (2016): Dwayne Johnson and Kevin Hart liked working together on Central Intelligence so much that they teamed up again for Jumanji.
Chappie (2015): Sharlto Copley played Chappie on set, and his performance was turned into the robot with computer effects.
Ninja and Yolandi, who play themselves in Chappie, are the South African rap group Die Antwoord.
Cheaper by the Dozen (2003): Cheaper by the Dozen is a remake of a 1950 movie, which was based on a real family with 12 kids.
Christopher Robin (2018): Jim Cummings voices both Winnie the Pooh and Tigger in Christopher Robin.
City of Ember (2008): City of Ember is based on Jeanne DuPrau's novel. The underground city was built inside a giant old shipyard building in Belfast.
Class Action Park (2020): Class Action Park is about the real Action Park in New Jersey, a water park famous for its wild rides.
Click (2006): Click was nominated for an Oscar for its makeup.
Clockstoppers (2002): Clockstoppers was directed by Jonathan Frakes, who played Commander Riker on Star Trek: The Next Generation.
Cold Pursuit (2019): Cold Pursuit is a remake of the Norwegian movie In Order of Disappearance, by the same director, Hans Petter Moland.
Coneheads (1993): Coneheads grew out of a Saturday Night Live sketch, and Dan Aykroyd and Jane Curtin played the same parts again.
Chris Rock: Bring the Pain (1996): Bring the Pain won Chris Rock two Emmy Awards.
Chris Rock: Tamborine (2018): Chris Rock: Tamborine was directed by Bo Burnham.
Chris Rock: Kill the Messenger (2008): Kill the Messenger was filmed in three cities, Johannesburg, London and New York, and edited together into one show.
Chris Rock: Selective Outrage (2023): Selective Outrage was the first comedy special Netflix ever streamed live.
Bill Burr: Paper Tiger (2019): Bill Burr filmed Paper Tiger at London's Royal Albert Hall.
Bill Burr: Live at Red Rocks (2022): Bill Burr filmed Live at Red Rocks at the famous outdoor theater in the rocks near Denver, Colorado.
All the Way (2016): Bryan Cranston plays President Lyndon B. Johnson in All the Way. He won a Tony Award for the same part on Broadway.
Always Be My Maybe (2019): Keanu Reeves plays a funny version of himself in Always Be My Maybe.
Allegiant (2016): Allegiant was meant to be followed by one more Divergent movie, but it was never made.
Constantine (2005): Constantine is based on the DC/Vertigo comic Hellblazer.
Tilda Swinton plays the angel Gabriel in Constantine.
Contagion (2011): The Contagion team worked with real disease experts, including scientists from the CDC, to make the outbreak believable.
Corpse Bride (2005): Corpse Bride was made with stop-motion puppets, moved by hand a tiny bit for every frame.
Johnny Depp and Helena Bonham Carter voice the two leads in Corpse Bride.
Crazy, Stupid, Love. (2011): Crazy, Stupid, Love. was the first of three movies Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone made together, before Gangster Squad and La La Land.
Cruella (2021): Cruella's costumes, more than 270 of them, were made by Jenny Beavan, who won an Oscar for them.
D.A.R.Y.L. (1985): D.A.R.Y.L. stands for Data Analyzing Robot Youth Lifeform.
Daddy's Home (2015): Will Ferrell and Mark Wahlberg had already played partners in the comedy The Other Guys before Daddy's Home.
Daddy's Home 2 (2017): Mel Gibson and John Lithgow join Daddy's Home 2 as the dads of the two dads.
Dark Shadows (2012): Dark Shadows is based on a 1960s daytime TV soap opera. Its original star, Jonathan Frid, has a cameo.
Dark Waters (2019): Dark Waters is based on the true story of lawyer Robert Bilott's fight against DuPont, told in a New York Times Magazine article.
Darkest Hour (2017): Gary Oldman spent about 200 hours in the makeup chair to become Winston Churchill, and won the Oscar for Best Actor.
Makeup artist Kazu Hiro came out of retirement to do Gary Oldman's Churchill makeup.
Date Night (2010): Date Night stars Steve Carell and Tina Fey, two of NBC's biggest sitcom stars at the time.
Dawn of the Planet of the Apes (2014): Andy Serkis played Caesar on location with motion-capture dots, so the apes were filmed in the real forest instead of a studio.
Death at a Funeral (2010): Death at a Funeral (2010) is a remake of a British movie from just three years earlier. Peter Dinklage plays the same part in both.
Death at a Funeral (2007): Death at a Funeral was directed by Frank Oz, the voice of Yoda and Miss Piggy.
Deck the Halls (2006): Deck the Halls stars Danny DeVito and Matthew Broderick as neighbors fighting over Christmas lights.
Deepwater Horizon (2016): The Deepwater Horizon crew built an almost full-size copy of the oil rig in a giant tank in Louisiana.
Defiance (2008): Defiance tells the true story of the Bielski brothers, who hid and protected more than 1,000 Jewish people in the forests of Belarus.
Despicable Me (2010): The Minions' language mixes words from Spanish, French, Italian, English and even food names.
The Minions are voiced by the directors, Pierre Coffin and Chris Renaud.
Despicable Me 3 (2017): In Despicable Me 3, Steve Carell voices both Gru and his twin brother Dru.
Despicable Me 4 (2024): Pierre Coffin still voices the Minions in Despicable Me 4, just as he did in the first movie.
Divergent (2014): Divergent is based on Veronica Roth's novel, which she wrote while still in college.
DodgeBall: A True Underdog Story (2004): Ben Stiller wore fake teeth and a fake mustache to play White Goodman in DodgeBall.
Real dodgeball coaches trained the DodgeBall cast for weeks.
Don't Look Up (2021): Some of Jonah Hill's lines in Don't Look Up were made up on the spot during filming.
Downsizing (2017): The tiny people in Downsizing were made by filming the actors on oversized sets and props.
Drumline (2002): The Drumline cast went to a drumming boot camp and learned to play for real.
Due Date (2010): Due Date was directed by Todd Phillips right after the first Hangover movie.
Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves: Many of the creatures in Honor Among Thieves were real puppets and costumes on set, not only computer effects.
Earth (2007): Earth was made from the same footage as the BBC series Planet Earth, narrated in the US by James Earl Jones.
Ella Enchanted (2004): Ella Enchanted is based on Gail Carson Levine's novel, which won a Newbery Honor.
Epic (2013): Epic is loosely based on William Joyce's picture book The Leaf Men and the Brave Good Bugs.
Eurovision Song Contest: The Story of Fi: Will Ferrell has been a fan of Eurovision since his wife's family in Sweden got him to watch it.
The song Husavik from the movie was nominated for an Oscar.
Evil Dead (2013): Evil Dead (2013) used almost no computer effects. Most of the blood and gore was real makeup and props.
Eye in the Sky (2015): Eye in the Sky was Alan Rickman's last on-screen role.
Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw (2: Hobbs & Shaw was the first spin-off from the Fast & Furious movies.
Finch (2021): Caleb Landry Jones played the robot Jeff on set in a motion-capture suit, often walking on stilts.
Flamin' Hot (2023): Flamin' Hot was Eva Longoria's first feature movie as a director.
Flight (2012): Flight was Robert Zemeckis's first live-action movie in 12 years, after Cast Away.
Flubber (1997): Flubber is a remake of Disney's 1961 movie The Absent-Minded Professor.
Fly Me to the Moon (2024): Fly Me to the Moon is named after the Frank Sinatra song, which became linked with the Apollo missions.
Four Brothers (2005): Four Brothers is loosely based on John Wayne's 1965 western The Sons of Katie Elder.
Fracture (2007): Fracture paired Anthony Hopkins with a rising Ryan Gosling.
Frequency (2000): Frequency was later turned into a TV series in 2016.
Frosty the Snowman (1969): Frosty the Snowman was made by Rankin/Bass, the studio behind Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer.
Comedian Jimmy Durante narrates and sings in Frosty the Snowman.
Fun with Dick and Jane (2005): Fun with Dick and Jane is a remake of a 1977 comedy with George Segal and Jane Fonda.
Fury (2014): Fury used a real Tiger tank from the Tank Museum in England, the first time a working Tiger appeared in a movie since World War II.
The Fury cast went through a tough army-style boot camp before filming.
Gamer (2009): Gamer was made by Neveldine and Taylor, the directors of the Crank movies.
Gangster Squad (2013): Gangster Squad is based on a real secret LAPD unit that fought gangster Mickey Cohen in the 1940s and 50s.
Gemini Man (2019): The young Will Smith in Gemini Man was made completely by computer, using Will Smith's own performance.
Get Smart (2008): Get Smart is based on the 1960s TV spy comedy created by Mel Brooks and Buck Henry.
Get Him to the Greek (2010): Russell Brand's Aldous Snow first appeared in Forgetting Sarah Marshall before getting his own movie.
Ghost in the Shell (2017): Ghost in the Shell is based on Masamune Shirow's manga and the classic 1995 anime movie.
Gifted (2017): Gifted was directed by Marc Webb, who also made The Amazing Spider-Man.
Going Clear: Scientology and the Prison: Going Clear won three Emmy Awards and is based on Lawrence Wright's book.
Gone in Sixty Seconds (2000): Gone in Sixty Seconds is a remake of a 1974 car-chase movie of the same name.
The star car, a 1967 Shelby Mustang named Eleanor, became famous on its own.
Grandma's Boy (2006): Grandma's Boy was made by Adam Sandler's company, Happy Madison.
Green Book (2018): Green Book won the Oscar for Best Picture. The Green Book was a real travel guide for Black drivers in the 1930s to 60s.
Greyhound (2020): Tom Hanks wrote the Greyhound screenplay himself, based on C.S. Forester's novel The Good Shepherd.
Parts of Greyhound were filmed on the USS Kidd, a real World War II destroyer that's now a museum.
Gridiron Gang (2006): Gridiron Gang is based on a real football team at a juvenile detention camp in California.
Gulliver's Travels (2010): Gulliver's Travels is a modern take on Jonathan Swift's 1726 novel.
Hanna (2011): The Chemical Brothers made the Hanna soundtrack.
Hardcore Henry (2015): Hardcore Henry was filmed almost entirely through GoPro cameras on a stunt person's head, so you see everything through Henry's eyes.
Harry and the Hendersons (1987): Rick Baker's Bigfoot suit for Harry and the Hendersons won the Oscar for Best Makeup.
Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Pa: Deathly Hallows: Part 2 was the last of the eight Harry Potter movies, made over about ten years with the same main cast.
Harvey (1950): Harvey is based on Mary Chase's play, which won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama.
Haunted Mansion (2023): Haunted Mansion is based on the Disneyland ride, which opened in 1969.
Hereditary (2018): Hereditary was Ari Aster's first feature movie as a director.
Hidden Figures (2016): Hidden Figures is based on Margot Lee Shetterly's book about real Black women mathematicians at NASA.
Hit Man (2023): Hit Man is loosely based on the real Gary Johnson, a Houston teacher who posed as a hitman for the police.
Glen Powell co-wrote Hit Man with director Richard Linklater.
Hitch (2005): Hitch was Will Smith's first romantic comedy.
Hocus Pocus 2 (2022): Hocus Pocus 2 came out 29 years after the first movie, with Bette Midler, Sarah Jessica Parker and Kathy Najimy back as the sisters.
Horrible Bosses (2011): Jennifer Aniston, Kevin Spacey and Colin Farrell play the three bosses. Colin Farrell came up with his character's comb-over look himself.
Hot Shots! (1991): Hot Shots! pokes fun at Top Gun and was co-written by Jim Abrahams, one of the Airplane! team.
Hubie Halloween (2020): Hubie Halloween was filmed in Massachusetts, around the real town of Salem.
Hustle (2022): Many real NBA players appear in Hustle, and the hero's discovery, Juancho Hernangómez, is a real NBA player.
I Am Mother (2019): The robot Mother was a real suit made by Weta Workshop, worn by actor Luke Hawker, and voiced by Rose Byrne.
The 6th Day (2000): The 6th Day has two Arnold Schwarzeneggers on screen at the same time.
The 7th Voyage of Sinbad (1958): The creatures in The 7th Voyage of Sinbad were brought to life by stop-motion legend Ray Harryhausen.
The Adam Project (2022): The Adam Project's script was around for years. Tom Cruise was once going to star in it.
The Adjustment Bureau (2011): The Adjustment Bureau is based on a Philip K. Dick short story, Adjustment Team.
The Ballad of Buster Scruggs (2018): The Ballad of Buster Scruggs started out as a planned TV series by the Coen brothers.
The Bank Job (2008): The Bank Job is based on a real 1971 London bank robbery, the Baker Street robbery.
The Batman (2022): The Batmobile in The Batman was a real working car built for the movie.
Much of The Batman's Gotham was made with giant LED screens behind the actors, like on The Mandalorian.
The Beekeeper (2024): The Beekeeper was written by Kurt Wimmer, who also wrote Equilibrium.
The Big Short (2015): The Big Short is based on Michael Lewis's book about the 2008 financial crash.
Adam McKay had celebrities like Margot Robbie break the fourth wall to explain tricky money ideas.
The Big Year (2011): The Big Year is about a real birdwatching contest, based on Mark Obmascik's book.
The Bob's Burgers Movie (2022): The Bob's Burgers Movie was made by the same voice cast and team as the TV show.
The Boondock Saints (1999): Writer-director Troy Duffy wrote The Boondock Saints while working as a bartender in Los Angeles.
The Boxtrolls (2014): The Boxtrolls was made by Laika, the stop-motion studio behind Coraline.
The Bucket List (2007): The Bucket List made the phrase bucket list popular around the world.
The Butler (2013): The Butler is inspired by Eugene Allen, who worked as a butler at the White House for 34 years.
The Butterfly Effect (2004): The Butterfly Effect is named after an idea in chaos theory: that a butterfly's wings could start a far-off storm.
The Cabin in the Woods (2012): The Cabin in the Woods was co-written by Joss Whedon and Drew Goddard in about three days.
The Cabin in the Woods was filmed in 2009 but sat on a shelf for about three years before release.
The Campaign (2012): The Campaign is Will Ferrell and Zach Galifianakis's first movie together.
The Core (2003): The Core is often named by scientists as one of the least realistic science movies ever made.
The Count of Monte Cristo (2002): The Count of Monte Cristo was filmed in Ireland and Malta, standing in for France.
The Country Bears (2002): The Country Bears is based on the Country Bear Jamboree, a show at Disney's theme parks.
The Courier (2021): The Courier tells the true story of Greville Wynne, a British businessman who carried secrets out of Moscow during the Cold War.
The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (200: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is based on an F. Scott Fitzgerald short story.
Benjamin Button won Oscars for makeup and for its visual effects.
The Disaster Artist (2017): The Disaster Artist is about the making of The Room, often called the best bad movie ever made.
James Franco directed The Disaster Artist while playing Tommy Wiseau, and stayed in character between takes.
The Do-Over (2016): The Do-Over was the second movie in Adam Sandler's big Netflix deal, after The Ridiculous 6.
The Drop (2014): The Drop was James Gandolfini's last movie. It's based on a short story by Dennis Lehane, who also wrote the script.
The Dukes of Hazzard (2005): The Dukes of Hazzard is based on the 1979 TV show. Lots of real Dodge Chargers were used, and many were wrecked doing jumps.
The Edge of Seventeen (2016): The Edge of Seventeen was Kelly Fremon Craig's first movie as a writer-director.
The Electric State (2025): The Electric State is based on Simon Stålenhag's illustrated novel, made of his paintings of giant robots in 1990s America.
The Endless (2018): Directors Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead also star in The Endless, playing brothers who share their own first names.
The Faculty (1998): The Faculty was directed by Robert Rodriguez and written by Kevin Williamson, the writer of Scream.
The Fog of War: Eleven Lessons from the: The Fog of War won the Oscar for Best Documentary. Errol Morris filmed it using his Interrotron, which lets people look straight into the camera.
The Foreigner (2017): The Foreigner is based on Stephen Leather's 1992 novel The Chinaman. Jackie Chan did his own stunts in his 60s.
The Game Plan (2007): The Game Plan was one of Dwayne Johnson's first family comedies, after his years as a wrestler.
The Gentlemen (2019): Guy Ritchie wrote and directed The Gentlemen, and later turned it into a Netflix series.
The Girl Who Leapt Through Time (2006): The Girl Who Leapt Through Time was directed by Mamoru Hosoda and is a sequel of sorts to a 1967 Japanese novel.
The Good Girl (2002): The Good Girl was written by Mike White, who later created The White Lotus.
The Great Outdoors (1988): The Great Outdoors was written by John Hughes and stars John Candy and Dan Aykroyd.
The Greatest Game Ever Played (2005): The Greatest Game Ever Played tells the true story of Francis Ouimet, an amateur golfer who won the 1913 US Open.
The Greatest Game Ever Played was directed by actor Bill Paxton.
The Green Hornet (2010): Seth Rogen co-wrote The Green Hornet with his longtime writing partner Evan Goldberg.
The Grey (2011): The Grey was filmed in freezing weather in British Columbia, and the actors' breath and shivering were real.
The Grinch (2018): Benedict Cumberbatch voices the Grinch with an American accent.
The Highwaymen (2019): The Highwaymen tells the story of Bonnie and Clyde from the side of the two Texas Rangers who hunted them.
The Host (2013): The Host is based on a novel by Stephenie Meyer, the author of Twilight.
The Hot Chick (2002): Rachel McAdams appears in The Hot Chick two years before Mean Girls.
The House with a Clock in Its Walls (201: The House with a Clock in Its Walls is based on John Bellairs's 1973 book and was directed by horror filmmaker Eli Roth.
The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 1 (2: The Hanging Tree song from Mockingjay - Part 1, sung by Jennifer Lawrence, became a real hit song.
The Hunt (2020): The Hunt was co-written by Damon Lindelof, who also made Lost and Watchmen.
The Hustle (2019): The Hustle is a remake of Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, which was itself a remake of the 1964 movie Bedtime Story.
2 Broke Girls (2011): 2 Broke Girls was co-created by Michael Patrick King, who also worked on Sex and the City.
3 Body Problem (2024): 3 Body Problem is based on Liu Cixin's award-winning Chinese novel trilogy.
3 Body Problem was made by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss, the creators of Game of Thrones.
Avenue 5 (2020): Avenue 5 was created by Armando Iannucci, who also made Veep.
Bar Rescue (2011): Jon Taffer, the host of Bar Rescue, says he came up with the idea behind NFL Sunday Ticket.
Barry (2018): Bill Hader co-created Barry and directed many episodes himself.
Henry Winkler won his first ever Emmy for playing acting teacher Gene Cousineau in Barry.
BEEF (2023): BEEF was inspired by a real road rage incident that happened to creator Lee Sung Jin.
Bill Nye: The Science Guy (1993): Bill Nye was a mechanical engineer at Boeing before becoming the Science Guy.
Bill Nye the Science Guy won 19 Emmy Awards.
Black Mirror (2011): Black Mirror is named after the dark, shiny screen of a phone or TV when it's turned off.
CatDog (1998): CatDog was created by Peter Hannan for Nickelodeon.
Cobra Kai (2018): Cobra Kai started on YouTube's paid service before moving to Netflix, where it became a huge hit.
Ralph Macchio and William Zabka play the same characters they played in The Karate Kid 34 years earlier.
Cosmos (2014): Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey was produced by Seth MacFarlane, the creator of Family Guy.
Neil deGrasse Tyson's Cosmos continues Carl Sagan's 1980 series, and Sagan's widow Ann Druyan co-wrote it.
Dark (2017): Dark was the first German-language series Netflix made.
Dark's young and old versions of each character were cast to look alike, sometimes matching eye colour with contact lenses.
Derry Girls (2018): Derry Girls is based on creator Lisa McGee's own teenage years in Derry, Northern Ireland, in the 1990s.
Dexter (2006): Dexter is based on Jeff Lindsay's novel Darkly Dreaming Dexter.
Dinosaurs (1991): Dinosaurs was made by Jim Henson's company, with actors inside large animatronic dinosaur suits.
Falling Skies (2011): Falling Skies was produced by Steven Spielberg.
Fleabag (2016): Fleabag started as a one-woman stage show by Phoebe Waller-Bridge at the Edinburgh Fringe festival.
For All Mankind (2019): For All Mankind was created by Ronald D. Moore, the man behind Battlestar Galactica and Outlander.
Forged in Fire (2015): Doug Marcaida's line 'It will keel' from Forged in Fire became a famous internet meme.

The giant spiral staircase in Silo was a real set, built several floors high.
Slow Horses (2022): Slow Horses is based on Mick Herron's Slough House novels.
Mick Jagger wrote and sings Slow Horses's theme song, Strange Game.
Snowfall (2017): Snowfall was co-created by John Singleton, the director of Boyz n the Hood, who grew up in Los Angeles in the 1980s.
Succession (2018): Jeremy Strong stayed deep in character as Kendall Roy for much of Succession.
Superstore (2015): Superstore creator Justin Spitzer also wrote for The Office.
Tales from the Loop (2020): Tales from the Loop is based on Simon Stålenhag's paintings of everyday life next to strange machines.
That '70s Show (1998): Mila Kunis lied about her age to get the part of Jackie in That '70s Show. She was 14, not 18.
That '70s Show began the careers of Ashton Kutcher, Mila Kunis and Topher Grace.
The Last Kingdom (2015): The Last Kingdom is based on Bernard Cornwell's Saxon Stories novels.
The Last Kingdom was filmed mostly in Hungary, standing in for England.
The Man in the High Castle (2015): The Man in the High Castle is based on Philip K. Dick's 1962 novel.
Ridley Scott was one of The Man in the High Castle's producers.
The Orville (2017): Seth MacFarlane created The Orville as a love letter to Star Trek, and many Star Trek veterans directed episodes.
The Righteous Gemstones (2019): Danny McBride created The Righteous Gemstones, and John Goodman plays the family's dad.
The Rookie (2018): The Rookie is loosely based on the true story of William Norcross, who joined the LAPD at age 45.
The Scooby-Doo Show (1976): The Scooby-Doo Show introduced Scooby's cousin Scooby-Dum.
The Smurfs (1981): The Smurfs began as Belgian comics by Peyo in 1958, and the cartoon was made by Hanna-Barbera.
In the original French, Smurfs are called Les Schtroumpfs.
The Terminal List (2022): The Terminal List is based on Jack Carr's novel. Carr is a former Navy SEAL and has a cameo in the show.
Tiger King (2020): Tiger King was one of Netflix's most-watched shows in spring 2020, as people stayed home during lockdown.
Tiger King's filmmakers spent about five years following the people in it.
Tokyo Vice (2022): Tokyo Vice is based on the memoir of Jake Adelstein, an American who became a crime reporter for a Japanese newspaper.
Michael Mann, the director of Heat, directed Tokyo Vice's first episode.
Tom Clancy's Jack Ryan (2018): John Krasinski is the fifth actor to play Jack Ryan, after Alec Baldwin, Harrison Ford, Ben Affleck and Chris Pine.
Trailer Park Boys (2001): Trailer Park Boys is filmed like a documentary in Nova Scotia, Canada, and started as a low-budget movie in 1999.
Travelers (2016) (2016): Travelers was created by Brad Wright, who also co-created Stargate SG-1.
Kitchen Nightmares (US) (2007): Kitchen Nightmares started in Britain as Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares before the American version.
Mr Inbetween (2018): Scott Ryan wrote every episode of Mr Inbetween and stars as Ray. It began as his low-budget 2005 movie The Magician.
The Imagineering Story (2019): The Imagineering Story was made by Leslie Iwerks, granddaughter of Ub Iwerks, who helped create Mickey Mouse.
Dark Matter (2015): Dark Matter began as a comic book by Joseph Mallozzi and Paul Mullie, writers on Stargate.
Dexter: Resurrection (2025): Dexter: Resurrection brings back Michael C. Hall as Dexter, plus guest stars like Uma Thurman and Neil Patrick Harris.
The Lazarus Project (2022): The Lazarus Project was written by Joe Barton, who also created Giri/Haji.
Ludwig (2024) (2024): Ludwig stars David Mitchell as a puzzle-maker pretending to be his twin brother, a police detective.
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure (2012) (2012): The JoJo's Bizarre Adventure manga started in 1987 and is still running.
Many JoJo powers are named after real bands and songs, like Killer Queen and Crazy Diamond.
Kaguya-sama: Love Is War (2019): Kaguya-sama's anime was made by A-1 Pictures, and its narrator's dramatic lines became famous with fans.
Mob Psycho 100 (2016): Mob Psycho 100 was created by ONE, the creator of One-Punch Man.
Mob Psycho 100's anime was made by studio Bones, known for hand-drawn fight scenes.
My Dress-Up Darling (2022): My Dress-Up Darling is based on Shinichi Fukuda's manga about a doll-maker and a cosplayer.
One-Punch Man (2015): One-Punch Man started as a free webcomic by ONE, drawn very roughly. Artist Yusuke Murata later redrew it as a polished manga.
One-Punch Man's first season was made by studio Madhouse.
Overlord (2015): Overlord is based on Kugane Maruyama's light novels, which started as a web novel.
Solo Leveling (2024): Solo Leveling began as a Korean web novel, then became a webtoon before the Japanese anime.
Solo Leveling's anime was made by A-1 Pictures, and its music was by Hiroyuki Sawano of Attack on Titan.
That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime started as a free web novel by Fuse.
The Seven Deadly Sins (2014): The Seven Deadly Sins is based on Nakaba Suzuki's manga, which ran in Weekly Shōnen Magazine.
Tokyo Revengers (2021): Tokyo Revengers is based on Ken Wakui's manga. Wakui was once a member of a youth gang himself.
Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters (2000): Yu-Gi-Oh! began as a manga by Kazuki Takahashi, and the card game in the story became a real card game.
The Yu-Gi-Oh! trading card game holds a Guinness World Record as one of the best-selling card games.
No Game No Life (2014): No Game No Life is based on light novels by Yū Kamiya, who also draws the illustrations.
Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senp: Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai is set in Fujisawa, Kanagawa, and fans visit its real locations.
Spice and Wolf: MERCHANT MEETS THE WISE: Spice and Wolf: Merchant Meets the Wise Wolf remakes the 2008 anime, with the same lead voice actors coming back.
So I'm a Spider, So What? (2021): So I'm a Spider, So What? started as a free web novel by Okina Baba.
Saga of Tanya the Evil (2017): Saga of Tanya the Evil is set in an alternate world that looks a lot like Europe in World War I.
Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? is often shortened by fans to DanMachi.
Log Horizon (2013): Log Horizon was written by Mamare Touno, who also wrote Maoyu: Archenemy & Hero.
Maoyu: Archenemy & Hero (2013): Maoyu began as a story posted on the Japanese message board 2channel.
GATE (2015): GATE was written by Takumi Yanai, a former member of Japan's Self-Defense Forces.
Grand Blue Dreaming (2018): Grand Blue Dreaming is written by Kenji Inoue, the author of Baka and Test.
Hinamatsuri (2018): Hinamatsuri is named after Japan's Girls' Day festival, held on March 3.
Gachiakuta (2025): Gachiakuta's graffiti art is designed by Hideyoshi Andou, a real graffiti artist who works on the manga.
Kengan Ashura (2019): Kengan Ashura began as a web manga on the Ura Sunday site.
MASHLE: MAGIC AND MUSCLES (2023): MASHLE's second season opening song, Bling-Bang-Bang-Born by Creepy Nuts, became a huge viral hit.
Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun (2019: Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun is based on Osamu Nishi's manga in Weekly Shōnen Champion.
Blue Box (2024): Blue Box is based on Kouji Miura's manga about a badminton player who has a crush on a basketball star.
Call of the Night (2022): Call of the Night is by Kotoyama, the creator of Dagashi Kashi, and is named after a Creepy Nuts song.
Campfire Cooking in Another World with M: Campfire Cooking in Another World started as a web novel by Ren Eguchi.
The Eminence in Shadow (2022): The Eminence in Shadow started as a free web novel by Daisuke Aizawa.
Basilisk (2005): Basilisk is based on Futaro Yamada's 1958 novel The Kouga Ninja Scrolls.
NANA (2006): NANA is based on Ai Yazawa's manga, which has been on pause since 2009.
Ninja Scroll: The Series (2003): Ninja Scroll: The Series follows the classic 1993 anime movie Ninja Scroll by Yoshiaki Kawajiri.
Snow White with the Red Hair (2015): Snow White with the Red Hair is based on Sorata Akiduki's manga.
Yona of the Dawn (2014): Yona of the Dawn is loosely inspired by Korea's ancient Goguryeo kingdom.
Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku (2018): Wotakoi started as a webcomic on the site Pixiv before becoming a manga.
Maid Sama! (2010): Maid Sama! is based on Hiro Fujiwara's manga, which ran in LaLa magazine.
Akagi (2005): Akagi was created by Nobuyuki Fukumoto, who also made Kaiji, and is about the tile game mahjong.
Fate/Grand Order - Absolute Demonic Fron: Babylonia is based on the mobile game Fate/Grand Order and features King Gilgamesh, from the oldest written story in the world.
The Ancient Magus' Bride (2017): The Ancient Magus' Bride is set in England and borrows from real British and Irish fairy folklore.
Love, Chunibyo & Other Delusions! (2012): Chūnibyō is a Japanese word for teens who act like they have secret powers, like a second-year middle schooler.
In Another World With My Smartphone (201: In Another World With My Smartphone started as a web novel by Patora Fuyuhara.
The Irregular at Magic High School (2014: The Irregular at Magic High School started as a web novel by Tsutomu Satō.
Reincarnated as a Sword (2022): Reincarnated as a Sword started as a web novel by Yuu Tanaka.
Seraph of the End (2015): Seraph of the End is based on a manga written by Takaya Kagami and drawn by Yamato Yamamoto.
My Happy Marriage (2023): My Happy Marriage was also made into a live-action Japanese movie in 2023.
ReLIFE (2016): ReLIFE started as a webcomic on the Comico app, and all 13 episodes were released online at once.
Recovery of an MMO Junkie (2017): Recovery of an MMO Junkie started as a webcomic on Comico.
The Testament of Sister New Devil (2015): The Testament of Sister New Devil is based on Tetsuto Uesu's light novels.
Sekirei (2008): Sekirei is based on Sakurako Gokurakuin's manga.
Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a: Sword Oratoria tells the DanMachi story from the side of Aiz Wallenstein and the Loki Familia.
Inside North Korea's Dynasty (2018): Inside North Korea's Dynasty is a National Geographic series about three generations of the Kim family.
